D1 Screening status. Spare Construct is a browser-based sketch and screening tool. It is not an approved regional transport model and it is not the Auckland Forecasting Centre Macro Strategic Model (MSM). Its results are indicative and are intended to scope, test and support a transport assessment. They must be reviewed, and where necessary confirmed with approved tools, by a suitably qualified transport planner or traffic engineer before they are relied on in any resource consent, plan change, notice of requirement, Fast-track application or funding decision.
sections.report-regulatory:
D10 Regulatory currency. Statutory references reflect the law and guidance as at 2026-10-08 for the pathway and lodgement date shown. Under the Planning Act 2026, consents lodged before 30 October 2026 are processed under the RMA as it stood immediately before 30 September 2026, and those lodged later are processed under the amended RMA as at lodgement. The specified transition date to the new planning system has not been set. This report is not legal or planning advice. Confirm the applicable provisions at lodgement.
D11 Authorities. Since 7 May 2026 Auckland Council is the road controlling authority for Auckland roads (Local Government (Auckland Council) Act 2009 s47), with local boards exercising specified powers on local and collector roads and Auckland Transport continuing as the transport CCO for public transport. AUP provisions that still refer to Auckland Transport are quoted as written. Confirm the reviewing and approving body for this application.
sections.report-model-status:
Model purpose: NZTA TMDG category E. The justification for this category has not been given (Settings › Calibration and validation › Why this category).

TMDG criteria are not a pass/fail checklist; meeting them does not by itself make a model fit for purpose (TMDG s5.8).
sections.report-scope:
Scope (NZTA RR 422 Table 6.1): Moderate, effects on a small area or neighbourhood.

A moderate scope is proportionate: net peak trips are 340 veh/h and no state highway is involved.
sections.report-limitations:
Spare Construct is a sketch model. Junction results are HCM 6 / Akcelik-based and indicative, not SIDRA output.

No SIDRA model was prepared for the Side 4 junction.
sections.report-exec:
• Pathway: Resource consent, lodgement 2026-11-03. Regime: RMA as amended by the Planning Act 2026, as at lodgement (Sch 1 cl 19, 21).
  • The development generates about 4 veh/h in the AM peak hour and 5 veh/h in the PM peak hour (vehicle trips, 2031, Option: signals at Side 2).
  • 3 junctions assessed; the highest degree of saturation is Main Road / Side 6N in the AM peak (DoS 0.68, LoS A). Indicative, not SIDRA output.
  • Extent of effects (AT ITA s4.2.1.1): AM peak 0 link directions and 0 junctions over the 5%/10% thresholds; PM peak 0 link directions and 0 junctions over the 5%/10% thresholds.
  • Crash history 2021–2025: 46 reported crashes in the downloaded CAS area, 17 fatal or serious (DSI).
  • Model status: AM Validated, PM Calibrated; every stored run converged.
  • The Side 2 signals are needed before the 200th dwelling.
  • Net 340 vehicle trips in the AM peak.
  • Side 2 signals needed.
sections.report-purpose:
This ITA supports a resource consent application for a mixed-use development.

It answers RMA s88(2)(b) & Schedule 4, and the tests in <E27>.
sections.report-reason:
• E27.6.1.1 trips over threshold
  • Parking infringement (E27.6.2)
  • Access location (E27.6.4)

The E27 screening table is added here by the compliance feature when it is installed. Never read an E27.6.1 exceedance by itself as requiring an ITA.
sections.report-rr422: Scope chosen: Moderate. The chosen scope's column is outlined.
sections.report-locality: The site is on the corner of "Main Road" and Side 2, 400 m from the town centre.
sections.report-zoning:
Operative AUP zone: Business - Mixed Use. Proposed PC120 rezoning to Residential - Terrace Housing.

The AUP zone map is added by the land-use feature when Auckland Unitary Plan zones are loaded.
sections.report-active:
Footpaths on both sides.
Shared path along Main Road (west).
sections.report-volumes: Weekday AM peak hour 07:45–08:45 (the busiest hour at 3 of 3 counts with a AM peak) and PM peak hour 16:30–17:30 (the busiest hour at 2 of 2 counts with a PM peak), derived from 5 counts of 6 NZTA and AT and Yours counts that report a peak hour (2023–2025).
sections.report-crashes:
Crash history from NZTA CAS for 2021 to 2025 plus 2026 to date. The tables use the five full years 2021–2025; the year to date is shown apart and is incomplete.

Most crashes at the Main Road / Side 2 priority junction involve right-turning vehicles.

D8 Safety. Crash histories are taken from NZTA CAS and the most recent months may be incomplete. Spare Construct's safety screening and audit briefing pack support, but do not replace, a Safe System Audit by an independent, qualified specialist, or sight distance assessment to Austroads Guide to Road Design Part 4A.
sections.report-receiving:
No permitted baseline scenario (RMA s104(2)) is set. If one is relied on, add a scenario with the role "Permitted baseline" so its effects are shown separately from the future receiving environment.

The Mill Road designation is included in the future baseline only where funded.
sections.report-access: Two vehicle accesses: a left-in left-out on Side 2 and a full-movement access on Side 4.
sections.report-accessibility:
Walking, cycling and public transport access is described in section 2.4, and levels of service in section 4.

Parking is provided at 1 space per dwelling plus 12 visitor spaces.
sections.report-staging-plan:
Build-out increments and the staging triggers are set out in section 5 (Table M2).

Build-out over three stages, each tied to the Side 2 upgrade.
sections.report-construction: Construction traffic will use Main Road between 7:00 am and 5:00 pm.
sections.report-scenarios:
Assessed in this report: Option: signals at Side 2 against Without development.

  • Check: Development is proposed development, but this is the existing scenario. Mark it committed (with its consent in the register) or remove it.
sections.report-modelling:
Spare Construct assigns peak-hour vehicle demand (gravity distribution with gateway through-traffic) to the network by conjugate Frank-Wolfe user equilibrium, with BPR link times (α 0.15, β 4) and HCM 6 / Akçelik junction delay. Background growth: compound, 2.0% a year from 2026. Convergence target: relative gap 0.010% with the TAG M3.1 stability rule, at most 200 iterations. Full inputs are in Appendix A.

Every stored run converged to its target (Appendix B).

MSM consistency checked (see Appendix B).

D7 Regional consistency. The AT ITA Guidelines 2025 v2 expect detailed modelling to be consistent with regional MSM forecasts where appropriate. Where this report states that MSM consistency was not checked, the forecasts should be reconciled with MSM or Auckland Forecasting Centre outputs before lodgement for any proposal with network-wide effects.
sections.report-walk: Pedestrian crossings are assessed against ANOP levels of service.
sections.report-extent: The extent sites are not stored on the scenario yet, so the assessed junctions are Spare Construct's own selection. Store the extent test (junctions feature) to use it for the SIDRA export and this report.
sections.report-junctions: The junction flow-scale test (+10% on every movement) follows this section, then turning movement diagrams for the key junctions; per-turn movement summaries are in Appendix C. The sensitivity pack (section 4.6) re-runs the whole network with trip rates and total demand ±10% and background growth ±50%.
sections.junctions-performance:
Junction flow-scale test (+10%)

No junction crosses its practical degree of saturation when flows rise by 10%.

Flow-scale test: TTOC-06 Traffic Signals Modelling Guidelines. Junctions are re-evaluated at flows × 1.10 with each run's signal timings; routes are not re-assigned. HCM 6 / Akcelik-based, indicative; not SIDRA output.
sections.junctions-turning:
Turning movement diagrams

Modelled peak-hour turning volumes, AM (PM), rounded to the nearest 5 veh/h. HCM 6 / Akcelik-based, indicative; not SIDRA output.
sections.report-safety:
Section 2.7 sets out the crash history for 2021–2025: 46 crashes, 17 of them fatal or serious.

A Stage 1 Safe System Audit is recommended before detailed design.

D8 Safety. Crash histories are taken from NZTA CAS and the most recent months may be incomplete. Spare Construct's safety screening and audit briefing pack support, but do not replace, a Safe System Audit by an independent, qualified specialist, or sight distance assessment to Austroads Guide to Road Design Part 4A.
sections.report-alignment: The proposal aligns with Future Connect and the RLTP.
sections.report-climate:
No climate hazard overlay is loaded for this project, so Spare Construct has not screened the network against flood, coastal inundation or slip hazards.

No flood hazard affects the access routes.
sections.report-sensitivity:
• No conclusion changes.
  • Growth <b>matters</b>.

Check the Side 2 result.
sections.report-economics: Indicative economics compare a transport option (the mitigation scenario) with the do-minimum (the scenario with the proposal), at the same travel demand. The development itself is not a transport option, so no benefit-cost ratio is given for it. Create a mitigation scenario (Scenarios › Create assessment set) or choose one in the Report tab.
sections.report-mitigation:
What each option changes against Without development:

  • Option: signals at Side 2: no network changes.

Signals at Side 2 are the preferred option; a roundabout was rejected on land take.
sections.report-staging:
The Side 2 signals are needed before the 200th dwelling.

  • Main Road / Side 2: AM: DoS 0.90 over 0.85 (new failure)
  • n2: LoS E
sections.report-conditions:
Staging condition from the staging test (section 5.2), for the author to confirm: The Side 2 signals are needed before the 200th dwelling.

A condition requiring the Side 2 signals before the 200th dwelling is proposed.

Travel plan monitoring one year after occupation.
sections.report-conclusion:
With the proposal, all 3 assessed junctions operate within practical DoS in the 2031 AM and PM peaks; the worst is Main Road / Side 6N (DoS 0.68, LoS A, AM peak). Junction results are indicative (HCM 6 / Akcelik-based), not SIDRA output.

Effects are avoided, remedied or mitigated.
sections.report-app-settings: These are every model setting used for the runs in this report, so a second user can reproduce them from the project file (project.corridor.json in the data pack). Values that differ from Spare Construct's current defaults are listed first, then every setting with the changed ones marked.
sections.report-app-calibration: D6 Calibration. Calibration and validation statistics are reported against the NZTA Transport Model Development Guidelines (2019) for the stated model purpose category. Those criteria are not a pass/fail checklist, and meeting them does not by itself make a model fit for purpose. Fitness for purpose is a judgment for the analyst and peer reviewer and, where NZTA is involved, NZTA's modelling specialists.

Standing disclaimers (version 2026-10-08)

D1 Screening status. Spare Construct is a browser-based sketch and screening tool. It is not an approved regional transport model and it is not the Auckland Forecasting Centre Macro Strategic Model (MSM). Its results are indicative and are intended to scope, test and support a transport assessment. They must be reviewed, and where necessary confirmed with approved tools, by a suitably qualified transport planner or traffic engineer before they are relied on in any resource consent, plan change, notice of requirement, Fast-track application or funding decision.
D2 Expert evidence. Spare Construct is not an expert witness and does not give opinions. Any person who relies on these outputs in evidence remains responsible for complying with the Code of Conduct for Expert Witnesses (Environment Court Practice Note 2023, section 9), including stating the assumptions and data relied on, the uncertainty in the results, and appropriate sensitivity and uncertainty analyses for any model. This report is DRAFT until adopted and signed by a named, suitably qualified author.
D3 Junction results. Junction delay, degree of saturation, level of service and queue results are calculated by Spare Construct using HCM 6 / Akcelik-based methods. They are indicative and are not SIDRA output. Any junction result relied on for a consent decision, signal design (ATOC Traffic Signals Design Guidelines) or condition should be confirmed in SIDRA or another tool accepted by the road controlling authority.
D4 Economics. The benefit-cost ratio is an indicative screening estimate following NZTA Monetised Benefits and Costs Manual v1.7.5 conventions. It is equivalent to an Indicative Efficiency Rating, not a funding-approval BCR. It is not MBCM-compliant unless the full procedures are applied to a model calibrated and validated to the NZTA Transport Model Development Guidelines and independently reviewed. IPM efficiency bands for 2027-30 are shown from NZTA's initial draft (August 2026) and may change after GPS 2027.
D5 ANOP. ANOP levels of service are indicative Spare Construct estimates. Confirm them in Auckland Transport's ANOP Assessment Tool using AT speed data before relying on them.
D6 Calibration. Calibration and validation statistics are reported against the NZTA Transport Model Development Guidelines (2019) for the stated model purpose category. Those criteria are not a pass/fail checklist, and meeting them does not by itself make a model fit for purpose. Fitness for purpose is a judgment for the analyst and peer reviewer and, where NZTA is involved, NZTA's modelling specialists.
D7 Regional consistency. The AT ITA Guidelines 2025 v2 expect detailed modelling to be consistent with regional MSM forecasts where appropriate. Where this report states that MSM consistency was not checked, the forecasts should be reconciled with MSM or Auckland Forecasting Centre outputs before lodgement for any proposal with network-wide effects.
D8 Safety. Crash histories are taken from NZTA CAS and the most recent months may be incomplete. Spare Construct's safety screening and audit briefing pack support, but do not replace, a Safe System Audit by an independent, qualified specialist, or sight distance assessment to Austroads Guide to Road Design Part 4A.
D9 Speed limits. This cost benefit disclosure statement follows the structure of clause 3.3 of the Land Transport Rule: Setting of Speed Limits 2024. It is not an MBCM benefit-cost ratio and cannot be used in place of MBCM procedures for NLTF funding.

AUP provisions that still refer to Auckland Transport are quoted as written. Confirm the reviewing and approving body for this application.

pack.data:
# Spare Construct is a browser-based sketch and screening tool. It is not an approved regional transport model and it is not the Auckland Forecasting Centre Macro Strategic Model (MSM). Its results are indicative and are intended to scope, test and support a transport assessment. They must be reviewed, and where necessary confirmed with approved tools, by a suitably qualified transport planner or traffic engineer before they are relied on in any resource consent, plan change, notice of requirement, Fast-track application or funding decision.
# Load Spare Construct ITA data pack CSVs in Python (standard library only).
# Every CSV is UTF-8 with a BOM, and its first row is Disclaimer D1: skip it.
# pandas: pd.read_csv(path, encoding='utf-8-sig', skiprows=1)
import csv, sys

def load(path):
    with open(path, encoding='utf-8-sig', newline='') as f:
        rows = list(csv.reader(f))
    if rows and rows[0] and rows[0][0].startswith('#'):
        rows = rows[1:]
    head, body = rows[0], rows[1:]
    return [dict(zip(head, r)) for r in body]

if __name__ == '__main__':
    path = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 'links.csv'
    data = load(path)
    print(f'{len(data)} rows from {path}')
    for row in data[:10]:
        print(row)
